title: Farfus wins at Oschersleben as title rivals fall away
dek: Augusto Farfus won at Oschersleben from second on the grid, 6.298 seconds ahead of Mike Rockenfeller, who left 33 points clear of Farfus as Spengler and Wickens collided out of the title fight.

chapters.title: Eight drivers, three races to go
text: The DTM returned after a four-week break for the eighth race of ten, held at the Motorsport Arena Oschersleben on Sunday 15 September over 51 laps of the 3.696-kilometre circuit. It followed the Nürburgring, where Robert Wickens had won in the rain from seventh on the grid, with Pascal Wehrlein's Mücke car setting the fastest lap, Christian Vietoris had completed the podium and Mike Rockenfeller, with fourth place, had pushed his lead out to 35 points. As there, the race called for two mandatory pit stops and a choice between option and standard tyres.

Rockenfeller therefore came to Saxony-Anhalt on 106 points, with Christian Vietoris second on 71, Wickens third on 70, Bruno Spengler fourth on 67, Augusto Farfus fifth on 66 and Gary Paffett sixth on 57. Eight drivers, the leader included, could still mathematically take the title with three races left and 25 points for each win. Spengler, the defending champion, was 39 points behind after two races without a point, in Moscow and at the Nürburgring, and Farfus was 40 adrift.

The Nürburgring had been a mixed weekend for BMW. Farfus started from pole and finished second, and Martin Tomczyk came from 20th on the grid to fifth for his first points of the season, but Spengler's damaged car left him 14th. Farfus himself had not won since the season-opening race at Hockenheim.

chapters.title: Spengler loses pole, Green inherits it
text: Qualifying was run in changeable, drizzly conditions that made timing the laps as important as speed. Six drivers, Vietoris, Mortara, Hand, Priaulx, Juncadella and Merhi, were out in the first part, and Wickens missed the cut for the third part of the session, lining up 11th.

Bruno Spengler produced the fastest lap in the four-car shoot-out, a 1:20.140, ahead of Jamie Green (1:20.263), Augusto Farfus (1:20.442) and Mike Rockenfeller (1:20.444). But the stewards moved him back five places, because his team had used in the third part of the session a tyre that was only permitted in the fourth. Spengler called the decision harsh, as the mistake had been the team's and gave him no advantage.

The penalty handed pole position to Green, with Farfus second and Rockenfeller third. Dirk Werner was fourth, Filipe Albuquerque fifth and Spengler sixth, ahead of Miguel Molina, Martin Tomczyk, Timo Scheider and Adrien Tambay in the top ten. Wickens was 11th, Paffett 12th, Mattias Ekström 13th and Pascal Wehrlein 14th, while Vietoris, second in the standings, started 20th.

chapters.title: Farfus gets the jump
text: The race was run in dry conditions. Farfus, starting from second, got away cleanly, passed Green on the way to the first corner and led from there. Spengler also made up places off the line from sixth.

Tomczyk, who had started eighth, jumped the start and had to take a drive-through penalty, which dropped him well down the field. Rockenfeller, who had started on standard tyres, slipped back to fourth in the early running. Hand, who had started 18th, would go on to set the fastest lap of the race on lap 14, a 1:21.255.

chapters.title: Options for Rockenfeller, damage for Spengler
text: Everyone had to make two mandatory stops, and the order of tyre compounds was the main strategic variable. Rockenfeller, on standard tyres to begin with, moved to the softer options and climbed to second, running faster on them than on the harder compound. Farfus stayed ahead of Rockenfeller through both rounds of stops.

Spengler could not match the leaders' pace with his BMW. His race ended in a collision with Wickens, whose Mercedes was also out: Wickens retired after 38 laps and Spengler after 40, 11 laps from the flag. Both drivers' title hopes ended there.
Further back, Scheider, who started ninth, worked his way forward to fifth with some forceful overtaking and Ekström, 13th on the grid, climbed to seventh.

chapters.title: Farfus holds Rockenfeller at bay
text: Farfus took the flag 6.298 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller for his second win of the season, with Green third, 6.912 seconds behind the winner. Albuquerque was fourth for Rosberg, 10.837 seconds back, and Scheider fifth. Paffett finished sixth, 14.707 seconds behind, the only Mercedes driver in the points.

All eight Audis finished in the top ten: after Ekström in seventh came Molina, Tambay and Mortara in eighth, ninth and tenth. Farfus was the only BMW driver in the points. Pascal Wehrlein was 11th, just outside the points, ahead of Marco Wittmann and Dirk Werner in 12th and 13th. Hand's fastest lap was not enough to lift him above 16th, and Tomczyk was classified 20th, two laps down.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller 33 clear with two races left
text: Farfus said his start had been the key to the win, as he took Green immediately, and that the stops were perfect too. He added that he still had a mathematical chance of the title and would fight for it. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt called the performance fantastic and said it was a great feeling to have a driver back on the top step, but admitted that given the grid positions BMW should have had one or two more cars in the points.

Rockenfeller said Farfus had been in a class of his own and that he had been faster on the option tyres than on the standards, which was why he was especially pleased with second place. He said he would like to win the title at Zandvoort and would be happy to wait until Hockenheim if that did not work out. Green said his race pace had been good and that he felt he should have done better than third. Audi's Dieter Gass called it a team result the squad had wished for, with all eight cars scoring.

The collision between Spengler and Wickens brought the sharpest words. Wickens said he had gone for the inside and that Spengler turned in on him, while Spengler said he had the better line and that Wickens had run into him. The stewards put the blame on Spengler and gave him a two-place grid penalty for the next race at Zandvoort. With Rockenfeller on 124 points, Farfus on 91, Vietoris on 71, Wickens on 70, Spengler on 67 and Paffett on 65, only Farfus could still catch the leader mathematically.

Audi's eight scorers meant it moved to within nine points of BMW in the manufacturers' table, 267 to 276, with Mercedes on 237. Albuquerque's fourth place brought him his first points of the season, while Mercedes had only Paffett in the points, in sixth after starting 12th. The weekend drew 70,500 spectators. The DTM next moved to Zandvoort for the ninth race on 29 September, where Rockenfeller could already clinch the title.

facts.v: Spengler set the fastest time in the shoot-out but was moved back five places for using a Q4-only tyre in Q3, so Green started from pole and Spengler from sixth.
